paragraphs.text: The proposal that neighbourhoods should make household waste sorting easier raises a useful question about sorting household waste. I agree with this view because it can meet a practical need. My support does not mean that every version of the proposal will work; the way it is introduced is also important.

paragraphs.label: Lý do 1 — lợi ích
paragraphs.text: One important point in favour of the proposal is that more recyclable material can be collected separately. This is possible because clear containers reduce the chance that paper and plastic become mixed with food waste. For example, a family can keep a small box for clean bottles instead of putting them in the same bag as dinner leftovers. The value of this example is that the benefit is connected with a real everyday need. It is easier for people to see the purpose of an approach when they can relate it to their own situation.

It is true that simple advice may overlook problems beyond a resident's control, especially because old pipes or shared building systems may require professional repairs. This calls for better planning rather than the complete rejection of the idea.

In conclusion, I support the view that communities should encourage practical water-saving habits. The main benefit is that people can avoid wasting treated water. However, careful planning and a response to practical difficulties are needed if that benefit is to be achieved.
